children: Ethereum price has recovered sharply over the past few days, but the rally has not yet produced the swing the bulls are waiting for. It climbed back above $2,500 after gaining nearly 5%, while the Bitcoin price moved above $82,000 as institutional demand returned to the crypto market. The divergence becomes clearer when observing the latest ETF flows, whale activity and on-chain data.

While traders are showing renewed buying interest, the underlying data does not confirm the broad demand required to sustain above $2,500 that may keep the token stuck below the range for a long time.
ETF Flows Show Bitcoin Receiving the Stronger Institutional Bid

Ever since institutions entered the crypto space, they have been largely influencing sentiment and, in turn, the prices of the top cryptos. In the current context, the decrease in the Ethereum ETF inflows can be considered one of the major reasons behind the ETH price weakness. Bitcoin ETFs have attracted nearly a billion since the start of the month, which supported the price in reclaiming $82,000.

On the other hand, Ethereum’s ETF activity has shown signs of strength, but it has been less consistent. The highest recorded figure in September is +$59.3K in inflows with few outflows, ending a 12-session inflow streak that bought more than a billion into the products.

These figures show that institutional investors have not abandoned ETH, but Bitcoin is currently receiving the more decisive and consistent institutional bid. Until these signals align, the latest ETH ETF rebound should be viewed as encouraging but incomplete. It does support the bullish case but does not prove that the ETH price is ready to move toward $3000.
ETH’s On-Chain Activity Is Not Confirming the Recovery

Ethereum’s latest on-chain data is one of the most important signals from the past 24 to 48 hours. The daily active addresses have not displayed any major variations, as they have been decreasing since 9th August. Moreover, the levels have remained below 500K this month and have also dropped by more than 5% compared to the levels it traded at during the previous year.

This suggests the ETH price is recovering, but network participation is not accelerating at the same pace. A sustained move toward $3000 would be more convincing if higher prices were accompanied by increasing wallet activity. Instead, the latest data shows a decline in active addresses, which does not necessarily point towards deteriorating fundamentals. A strong breakout above the pivotal resistance may attract more activity.
Whale Activity is High, But It Does Not Mean Accumulation

Ethereum whale activity has also intensified over the past few days. The latest Ethereum whale tracker shows more than a million ETH involved, representing nearly $5 billion in transaction volume across 650 transactions in the past couple of days. One whale reportedly moved more than 70K ETH, worth $174 million, into exchanges over 48 hours, while retaining another 97,114 ETH.

Large ETH movements can represent exchange transfers, institutional custody movements, wallet restructuring, over-the-counter settlements, or actual buying and selling. If those deposits were intended for sale, the transfer could create additional short-term supply as ETH approaches resistance. Hence, the whale data should be interpreted as elevated positioning and potential supply movement, rather than clear evidence of accumulation.
The $2,500 to $2,550 Zone is Still a Real Test

The ETH price rallied roughly 5% and reclaimed $2,500; however, the $2,560 region has repeatedly capped upside attempts. The latest technical setup identifies $2,560 as the level ETH needs to clear before the rally can extend toward $2,600 and potentially higher.

The weekly RSI has moved above the average range, suggesting the momentum has turned consecutive. Besides, the volume profile adds another layer to the setup, as the price is trading within a relatively active volume area around $2000 to $2500. This suggests there is substantial historical trading activity around this range. Therefore, a sustained move above this range would take ETH above the consolidated range and bring the $3000 target back into focus.
Ethereum Price Prediction: Can ETH Reach $3000?

Ethereum’s setup remains cautiously bullish, but the latest data does not yet justify calling $3000 the next immediate target. Stronger BTC ETF demand, softer Ethereum network participation and mixed whale flows suggest that ETH still needs a broader demand catalyst. Technically, the $2500 and $2650 resistance zones remain the key hurdle, and a decisive breakout could open the path toward $3000 and extend to the $3300 to $3500 range. Until then, another rejection could leave ETH vulnerable to a move back toward the $2,000 to $ 2,100 range.

title: Why Is Ethereum Still Below $3000? While Bitcoin Price Hits $82,000—Here’s What You Need to Know
